issues.title: Finite-basis chaos projection does not commute with Malliavin differentiation
issues.failure_explanation: Let h1 and h2 be orthonormal, retain only h1, and take F=B(h1)B(h2), P=2, M=1 and k=1. The finite-basis projection of F is zero, so D_s C^{2,1}(F)=0. But D_sF=h1(s)B(h2)+h2(s)B(h1), and its finite-basis first-chaos projection is h2(s)B(h1), which is nonzero wherever h2(s) is nonzero. Hence the claimed finite-basis commutation fails even a.e., independently of the separate issue that Malliavin derivatives are only defined up to null sets.
issues.overall_effect: The supporting lemma contains a false identity, and the old Malliavin-energy proof lacks a valid stated basis for the finite-projection derivative contraction used at the terminal condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false finite-basis commutation equality by the correct Hilbert-valued projection formula. If Π_M denotes orthogonal projection onto span{h_1,…,h_M}, then, with the chaos projection acting on the random coordinates, state D^k C_tau^{P,M}(F)=Π_M^{⊗k}C_tau^{P-k,M}(D^kF) almost everywhere. In particular, prove E||D C_tau^{P,M}(F)||²≤E||DF||² and use this contraction at the terminal step of the Malliavin-energy argument; the dependent estimates can then retain their stated rates.
issues.why_classification: The old pointwise equality is a coherent but false structural claim, not a transcriptional error. Correcting it requires a vector-valued projection argument and materially qualifies the asserted commutation property. This is a contained, nontrivial repair with only limited loss, and it restores the affected energy and truncation bounds without global reconstruction.

issues.title: Exact-coefficient implementation proof uses invalid endpoint indices
issues.failure_explanation: The mesh increments are defined only for indices 1 through m, but the lemma assumes a maximum beginning at i=0. Its proof then defines I_i through an integral over [t_i,t_{i+1}] for i=0,…,m and applies the averaged-Z recurrence through i=m. Thus I_m, t_{m+1}, and Δ_{m+1} are undefined. The convention that the terminal averaged Z equals zero requires a separate terminal step rather than the interior estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete Gronwall and summed energy argument proving the exact implementation-error estimate is not well-defined at the terminal endpoint.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Index the mesh-ratio condition only over 1≤i≤m−1, define I_m solely as the terminal Y-error, and define interval energies only for 0≤i≤m−1. Apply the averaged-Z estimate and interior recurrence only through i=m−1; use the convention that both terminal averaged-Z variables vanish to derive a separate i=m inequality before applying discrete Gronwall and summing the energies.
issues.why_classification: The proof actually invokes undefined endpoint objects, so this is not merely a typographical index slip. Nevertheless, the terminal convention gives an immediate local case split, after which the same Gronwall argument, estimate, constants, and dependent theorem guarantees survive unchanged.

issues.title: Malliavin-energy proof differentiates a recursion not satisfied by the scheme
issues.failure_explanation: The old paper's own stepwise projection remark gives C^{P,M(i)}(F_i)=Y_{t_i}^{π,θ}+Δ_i C^P(f_i^{π,θ}). For a nonlinear generator, f_i^{π,θ} need not have chaos order at most P, so C^P(f_i^{π,θ}) cannot be replaced by f_i^{π,θ}. The proof nevertheless differentiates precisely that false unprojected identity. It also applies the ensuing averaged-Z recurrence at the first endpoint where Δ0 and the corresponding averaged Z are not defined. The new proof uses the projected identity, derivative contraction, and separate endpoint handling.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform Malliavin-energy estimates, and hence the chaos-order truncation terms in both main theorems, are not established by the old proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Differentiate the recursion actually satisfied by the projected scheme, namely Y_{t_{i-1}}^{π,θ}+∫Z^{π,θ}dB=Y_{t_i}^{π,θ}+Δ_i C^P(f_i^{π,θ}). Bound the resulting projected derivative by the valid full-chaos contraction E||D C^P(f_i^{π,θ})||²≤E||Df_i^{π,θ}||², and then run the existing chain-rule, Young-inequality, and Gronwall estimates. Restrict the averaged-Z recurrence to i=2,…,m and control the i=1 term directly so that no Δ_0 or averaged Z_0 is used.
issues.why_classification: The correct projected recursion is already supplied by the old source, and the needed full-chaos derivative contraction follows routinely from its valid chaos-order properties. Substituting that identity and separating the first endpoint are short local repairs that preserve the Malliavin-energy lemma and both downstream rates without a new proof architecture or substantive weakening.

issues.title: Malliavin-energy lemma omits its small-mesh hypothesis
issues.failure_explanation: The old lemma presents its two energy inequalities without restricting π. In the proof, ε is fixed in terms of L and the derivative bound of f, after which the argument assumes |π|≤min(1,ε) to obtain the coefficient Δ_i/(2L) and close the discrete recursion. Consequently, the proof supports the lemma only for sufficiently small meshes.
issues.overall_effect: The energy estimate and the main truncation bounds inherit a small-mesh regime that the old lemma did not state.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the Malliavin-energy lemma only for |π| below a threshold determined by L and the bound on the derivatives of f, as required by the absorption step, and carry that threshold into every dependent invocation. Keep the same constants and conclusions within this sufficiently fine-mesh regime.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine omitted premise because the proof uses the smallness assumption to close its recursion. The threshold is explicitly supplied by the existing argument and is a standard local stability qualification; it leaves the method, estimates, and asymptotic rates unchanged in their intended fine-mesh regime.

issues.title: Monte Carlo implementation proof uses invalid terminal indices
issues.failure_explanation: The old mesh increments exist only for indices 1,…,m, but the lemma's ratio begins at i=0. More importantly, the proof states the recurrence tagged main inequality theorem our error 2 for i=1,…,m after bounding the averaged-Z error by an integral over [t_i,t_{i+1}] divided by Δ_{i+1}. At i=m these objects are undefined. Since both terminal averaged-Z variables are zero, the terminal case must instead be estimated before that interior bound is used.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete Gronwall and energy summation used to prove the Monte Carlo coefficient-error estimate are not valid as written at the terminal step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Index the mesh-ratio condition over 1≤i≤m−1, define I_m as the terminal coefficient-projection error without a following Z-interval, and apply the averaged-Z inequality and interior recurrence only for i=1,…,m−1. Since both terminal averaged-Z variables are zero, derive the i=m estimate directly and then combine it with the interior recurrences in the same Gronwall and energy summation.
issues.why_classification: The old proof uses undefined terminal intervals and increments, so an inference rather than mere typography must be repaired. The zero terminal convention supplies a routine one-step case split, preserving the Monte Carlo estimate and its dependent main theorem with no new lemma, rate loss, or scope change.

issues.title: Main error theorems are stated under insufficient regularity assumptions
issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims its bounds under Assumption 1, which gives only ξ∈L2 and Lipschitz regularity of f. The bound itself contains the Malliavin quantity E||Dξ||², the implementation analysis uses Malliavin-energy estimates requiring differentiability, and the |π| term comes from Theorem main convergence rate, which assumes ξ∈D^{2,q}, q>4, Malliavin Hölder bounds, and a smoother time-regular deterministic generator. Thus the old paper claims the estimates on a substantially larger class than its formal chain establishes; Assumption 1 also does not imply the fourth moment asserted in the following remark.
issues.overall_effect: Neither main implementation-error theorem is established for arbitrary square-integrable terminal conditions and merely Lipschitz generators as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate both main error theorems under the full hypotheses used by their proof: the Malliavin-regular terminal condition and smooth, time-regular deterministic generator of Assumption main convergence rate, together with boundedness of f for the Monte Carlo theorem and the additional kernel condition where invoked. Remove the assertion that Assumption 1 implies a fourth moment and instead derive that moment from the q>4 hypothesis.
issues.why_classification: The only concrete source-supported repair preserves the displayed bounds by restricting arbitrary L² terminal data and merely Lipschitz generators to a substantially smaller Malliavin-smooth and generator-smooth class. That excludes a natural and prominently advertised input regime and therefore causes major scope loss across both main theorems. Retaining the weak hypotheses and the same rates would require essentially new convergence and Malliavin analysis not established in the source, so no complete route avoids either major loss or global reconstruction.

issues.title: Main error estimates omit the proved small-mesh regime
issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims a constant independent of π for every partition satisfying the stated ratio condition. Its |π| contribution comes from Theorem main convergence rate, which applies only below a threshold, and the implementation lemma likewise assumes a sufficiently small mesh after an explicit absorption step. Thus the old argument establishes the displayed estimate only for sufficiently small |π|, not over the unrestricted partition regime stated.
issues.overall_effect: The two main estimates overstate the mesh regime supported by their proof, although their asymptotic convergence rates remain valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to both main error theorems a condition |π|<η, where η is no larger than the thresholds in the Euler convergence theorem and the applicable implementation and energy lemmas. State that η and the error constant are independent of π and of the truncation or Monte Carlo parameters.
issues.why_classification: The missing qualification is mathematically required, so it is not a typo. It is nevertheless a local, source-supported fine-mesh condition: the same conclusions, parameter rates, and asymptotic convergence guarantees remain valid, with only unsupported coarse partitions removed.
